title: A counterexample to Wall's D(2) problem
description: Wall's finite D(2) problem: is a finite complex of dimension three that looks two-dimensional to homology and cohomology with all coefficients homotopy equivalent to a finite complex of dimension two? Chain complexes twisted by a character of the fundamental group; Fox derivatives; an obstruction for complexes of dimension two proved by a tower of infinite cyclic covers; the finite plus construction; an explicit group that gives a counterexample. The new arguments are proved in full; six standard theorems of algebraic topology are named hypotheses. The course is an exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026).

units.title: Wall's D(2) problem and twisted homology

prerequisites: core course Algebraic Topology (D60): CW complexes, fundamental group, covering spaces, homology
groups, group rings and modules; tensor products over a ring
six standard theorems of algebraic topology are named hypotheses of the course (TOP1 to TOP6 in the first lesson); everything else is proved in the four lessons
